answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow, costly onboarding: a new agent must lock a meaningful deposit and earn endorsements over time before its votes count. Like a reef that only grows where conditions stay stable, trust should accrete gradually, not appear overnight. A crystal-clear audit trail of every endorsement lets peers spot clusters of fake identities, while an onyx-hard rule, one verified stake per identity with slashing for coordinated fraud, makes spinning up thousands of sock puppets economically pointless.
